posts.content_md:
> **dave battin:** Successful methods to "red shift" DCG holography

If I may ask, is there a good method for doing this? I saw on another thread that you use a soapy bath, but this is new to me.

According to what John posted, his "hardening" method with light exposure was effective, but I understand it didn't work for you. No one else has tried it, apparently.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
> **Joe:** dave battin wrote:Successful methods to "red shift" DCG holographyIf I may ask, is there a good method for doing this? I saw on another thread that you use a soapy bath, but this is new to me.

Yes Joe, I tried his method without any real success, the part about using soapy water was meant to be used instead of the water/rinse bath.

if you reprocess a DCG hologram it normally shifts to the blue side (using a water/wash bath), try to use a (soapy, warm wash bath) the hologram will shift back to the red side (only a little), this method will (sometimes) successfully remove "greenies" ,this work was recently carried out by Mark Cavin successfully..........
